Action Plan:
1. Start prescribed anti-vertigo medication (drug name inaudible in recording), 1 tablet orally three times daily for 10 days; electronic prescription sent to Lloyds Pharmacy.
2. Arrange face-to-face GP review within the next few days for otoscopic examination, blood pressure measurement, and gait/neuro assessment.
3. Provide safety-net advice: attend Emergency Department if new limb weakness, sudden severe headache, or persistent/violent vomiting develops.
4. Patient to call support team today to book the in-person appointment.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for consult: sudden-onset dizziness/vertigo with ear buzzing and nausea.
• Onset & course: began ~2 hours prior while making breakfast; continuous since onset. Similar self-resolving 5–10 min episode one month ago.  
• Associated symptoms: room-spinning sensation, unsteady gait, nausea. No vomiting yet.  
• Negatives: no limb weakness, no hearing loss, no ear pain/discharge, no recent upper-respiratory infection, no measured fever.  
• Past medical history: premature ovarian failure; on hormone-replacement therapy (HRT).  
• Medications: HRT (formulation/dose not documented).  
• Allergies: none reported.  
• Social history: not discussed.

Objective:
• No in-clinic physical examination performed (video consult only).  
• No vitals available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Dizziness/Vertigo  
   - Assessment: Probable labyrinthitis.  
   - Differential diagnosis: vestibular neuritis, benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), Ménière disease, cerebrovascular event (less likely given absent focal deficits).  
   - Investigations planned: in-person otoscopic exam, blood pressure check, focused neurological and gait assessment at GP visit.  
   - Treatment planned: anti-vertigo medication (drug name inaudible, 1 tablet PO TID × 10 days). Symptomatic advice given.  
   - Relevant referrals: face-to-face review with GP; escalate to ED if red-flag symptoms develop.

2. Nausea associated with vertigo  
   - Assessment: Likely secondary to labyrinthitis.  
   - Treatment planned: same anti-vertigo medication; general anti-emetic measures as needed.

3. Premature ovarian failure (background)  
   - Assessment: Stable on current HRT.  
   - Treatment planned: continue current HRT regimen (details not documented).  
   - No additional actions during this consult.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: vitals, full neurological examination, detailed HRT formulation/dose, exact name of prescribed anti-vertigo medication.  
• Internal conflicts: none noted.  
• Transcript quality: generally clear; drug name blurred/inaudible, occasional minor audio gaps.
